name: Apple
grown_as: Fruit trees on rootstocks, both eating, cooking and cider apples ('Spartan', 'Jonagold', 'Rode Boskoop', 'Bramley's Seedling', 'Fair Maid of Devon', 'Slack-ma-Girdle', 'Dufflin', 'Pendragon' and others in William's list). They differ in fruit colour and tree vigour; leaf and blossom are much the same. 'Pendragon' has red-tinged leaves, bark and flowers.
habit: A small deciduous tree with a rounded, spreading crown; 2 to 4 m on dwarfing rootstocks, 6 to 9 m as a standard orchard tree. Grey-brown bark, smooth when young, later scaly. Fruit and flowers come from short, knobbly spurs along the older branches.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate on long shoots; in tufts of three to six on the spurs, with the flowers
leaf.outline: Oval to elliptic, 5 to 10 cm long, about half as wide
leaf.margin: Finely and bluntly toothed (small rounded or slightly pointed teeth) all the way round, never lobed
leaf.veins: A midrib and 4 to 7 pairs of side veins that curve forward towards the tip, lightly pressed in
leaf.surface: Dull mid green above, a little downy at first; paler, grey-green and softly woolly beneath, the felt clearest on young leaves
leaf.stalk: 1.5 to 3 cm, downy, with two tiny thread-like stipules at its base
leaf.colour: Mid green above, grey-green beneath; yellow in autumn

flower.form: An open, shallow cup like a large wild rose
flower.petals: Five, free, broad and rounded, slightly cupped, narrowing to a short claw
flower.colour: White inside, flushed pink on the back; the buds are deep pink and the flowers fade whiter as they age
flower.centre: About twenty stamens with yellow anthers around five pale green styles joined at the base
flower.behind: Five narrow, pointed, woolly grey-green sepals, turned back
flower.carried: In clusters of four to six at the tip of each spur, among a tuft of young leaves; the middle (king) flower opens first, the others on longer stalks around it, facing up and out

fruit: A pome: round to slightly flattened, 5 to 10 cm (cider apples often 3 to 5 cm), with the stalk sunk in a hollow at the top and the dried sepals forming a little crown (the eye) in a hollow at the bottom. Colour by variety: green ('Bramley's Seedling'), yellow, or flushed and striped red over yellow-green. Hangs on a short stalk, singly or two or three together. Ripe September to October. Fruit set: small green fruitlets in clusters at the spur tips, upright at first, each with the dried sepals at its tip; some drop in June.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as grafted trees
winter: Bare tree. Grey-brown branches with short knobbly spurs; fat, rounded, downy buds on the spurs (flower buds) and smaller pointed buds pressed against the shoots. Young shoots grey and woolly at the tips.

leaf: simple oval leaf with a short pointed tip, not lobed
fine blunt teeth all round the edge
paler, woolly underside if the back shows
bloom: five broad rounded petals, white with a pink flush on the back
a deep pink bud beside it
young: a single straight trunk with a few spreading branches
dormant: bare branches with short knobbly spurs
flower: clusters of pink-backed white blossom with pink buds on the spurs
flowers open with the young leaves, not before them
set: small green fruitlets in clusters at the spur tips
dried sepals visible at the tip of each fruitlet
crop: round apples with the stalk in a hollow, hanging on short stalks
red-flushed fruit among simple oval leaves

look_alikes: Pear blossom is pure white with dark red-purple anthers, and the leaves are glossy, rounder and on longer stalks. Crab apple (Malus sylvestris) has smaller sour fruit, 2 to 3 cm, and leaves that lose their hairs. Plum and cherry flowers have a single style in the centre, not five, and come in small bunches straight from the wood.
